content: 1. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir through mechanisms involving P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Close monitoring is required, and caution should be exercised. Dose reduction of P-gp substrates may be necessary if minimal concentration changes could lead to serious adverse reactions. 2. Darolutamide, a BCRP inhibitor, increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir. Avoid coadministration with BCRP inhibitors if possible. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of BCRP substrate drugs. 3. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Eliglustat increases sofosbuvir levels through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor therapeutic drug concentrations or consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates. 5. Sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Encorafenib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir. Monitor for signs of increased exposure and consider adjusting the dose of BCRP substrates. 7. Erdafitinib increases sofosbuvir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 8. Fosphenytoin decreases sofosbuvir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters, reducing conversion to its active metabolite (GS-331007), which is responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Fostemsavir, a BCRP inhibitor, increases sofosbuvir levels. Avoid coadministration if possible or modify the dose of BCRP substrates. Monitor closely. 10. Istradefylline increases sofosbuvir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. 11. Lasmiditan increases sofosbuvir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Leniolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 13. Lonafarnib, a weak P-gp inhibitor, increases sofosbuvir levels. Monitor for adverse reactions and reduce the dose of P-gp substrates if needed. 14. Mavorixafor, a P-gp inhibitor, increases sofosbuvir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. 15. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases sofosbuvir toxicity by competing for plasma protein binding. Monitor closely and adjust the dose of BCRP substrates if necessary. 16. Otesaconazole, a BCRP inhibitor, increases sofosbuvir levels. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider reducing their dose. Monitor closely. 17. Oxcarbazepine decreases sofosbuvir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters, reducing conversion to its active metabolite (GS-331007). Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Phenobarbital decreases sofosbuvir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters, reducing conversion to its active metabolite (GS-331007). Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Safinamide, which may inhibit intestinal BCRP, increases sofosbuvir levels. Monitor BCRP substrates for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. 25. Sarecycline increases sofosbuvir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Dosage reduction of P-gp substrates may be required. 26. Sotorasib decreases sofosbuvir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If use is unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage modifications. 27. Stiripentol, a BCRP transport inhibitor, increases sofosbuvir levels. Consider dosage reduction for BCRP substrates if adverse effects occur. Monitor closely. 29. Tafamidis, a BCRP inhibitor, increases sofosbuvir levels. Dosage adjustment of BCRP substrates may be necessary. Monitor closely. 30. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. 33. Vadadustat increases sofosbuvir levels by increasing exposure to BCRP substrates. Monitor for signs of adverse effects and reduce substrate dose as per product labeling. 36. Patients should be tested for current or prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection before initiating treatment with hepatitis C virus (HCV) direct-acting antivirals (DAAs). HBV reactivation has been reported in HCV/HBV coinfected patients undergoing or completing DAA treatment without HBV antiviral therapy. Some cases have resulted in fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, and death. Monitor for hepatitis flare or HBV reactivation during and after HCV treatment. Initiate appropriate management for HBV infection as clinically indicated. 37. Sofosbuvir must not be used as monotherapy. Combination therapy with ribavirin or peginterferon alfa and ribavirin is contraindicated in pregnant women and in men whose female partners are pregnant. Refer to ribavirin and/or peginterferon alfa prescribing information for risks during pregnancy. 38. There is no adequate human data to establish whether sofosbuvir poses a risk to pregnancy outcomes. It is unknown whether sofosbuvir or its metabolites are present in human breast milk, affect milk production, or have effects on breastfed infants. The predominant circulating metabolite of sofosbuvir (GS-331007) was observed in the milk of lactating rats without effects on nursing pups. The benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for therapy and potential adverse effects on the breastfed child. 39. Sofosbuvir is a nucleotide prodrug metabolized to an active uridine analog triphosphate, which inhibits HCV NS5B RNA-dependent polymerase, suppressing viral replication. Data on genotype 5 or 6 HCV infection is insufficient for dosing recommendations. For genotypes 2 or 3, the addition of peginterferon alfa to sofosbuvir/ribavirin therapy did not significantly improve sustained virologic response (SVR) compared to sofosbuvir/ribavirin alone. 40. Oral pellets should not be chewed. If administered with food, sprinkle on nonacidic soft food (e.g., pudding, chocolate syrup, mashed potato, ice cream) at or below room temperature. Consume within 30 minutes of mixing without chewing to avoid a bitter aftertaste. Store tablets and oral pellet packets below 30°C. Do not use packets if the seal is broken or damaged.
